summary: Fourteen-day Nightscout review with 98.7% CGM coverage, mean glucose 121.6 mg/dL, TIR 86.0%, TBR 5.1%, and CV 32.6%. The selected AAPS profile is complete and declared applicable. No carb entries were recorded, so the loop ran with COB 0 and used always-on SMB plus UAM as the meal system. Afternoon highs and evening or overnight lows share several plausible causes and do not support an isolated profile or automation change.

analysis_steps.findings: CGM quality is good enough for pattern review. The authoritative aaps_profile is complete. Carb telemetry is empty, and a mid-period profile switch, u200 dilution note, GLP-1 notes, site and sensor changes, and a pump occlusion reduce regime uniformity.
analysis_steps.evidence: 3995 valid entries, 98.7% coverage, 10 gaps, largest gap 65 minutes, 0 invalid or duplicate readings. Treatments include 655 insulin entries and 0 carb entries. Profile context historical applicability is yes. Events include a 13 Aug profile switch to u200 dilute basal 16-2u per day FLAT ISF, GLP-1 1.25 mg notes, and 19 Aug occlusion.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: No activity log, no full treatment or loop-status archive, and no historical profile object from before the 13 Aug switch.

analysis_steps.findings: The binding safety constraint is recurrent hypoglycemia, not mean glucose. Local evening and early-night hours carry the most time below range. Severe lows reached 41 to 42 mg/dL. High IOB samples and large post-correction drops show stacking risk.
analysis_steps.evidence: Overall TBR 5.1%, TAR 8.9%, lows on 13, 14, and 21 Aug. Local TBR 18.5% at hour 1 and 15.3% at hour 19. Local TAR 32.1% at hour 16. Sampled IOB 4.73 U and 5.935 U. Some correction windows fell 108 to 178 mg/dL by 120 minutes.
analysis_steps.dependencies: data_quality, including zero carb logging and mid-period therapy changes.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: No hypo-treatment log and no exercise annotation.

analysis_steps.findings: Overnight hours 4 to 7 look stable and do not show a classic under-basal dawn. Hours 0 to 3 sit near the 90 mg/dL target with high TBR, which is more consistent with residual evening IOB than with 0.6 U/h being proven too high. Afternoon TAR occurs while basal falls to 0.5 U/h but is not a fasting basal test. Evening basal 0.7 U/h is a possible co-factor after daytime highs.
analysis_steps.evidence: Basal 0.6, 0.7, 0.8, 0.7, 0.5, 0.6, then 0.7 U/h. Targets 90, 100 from 08:00, and 90 from 23:00. Local hours 4 to 7 TIR 95 to 99%. Local hours 14 to 16 averages 148 to 163 mg/dL. Lows clustered after afternoon peaks on 13 and 14 Aug.
analysis_steps.dependencies: safety_overview hypo cap; data_quality because observed glucose is closed-loop, not raw profile basal.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: No fasting basal test windows and no pre versus post 13 Aug basal comparison.

analysis_steps.findings: CR segments were not exercised. Flat ISF 56 cannot be estimated from the correction windows because those windows include food-like rises, SMB, and Dynamic ISF. DIA 10 h is compatible with an overnight insulin tail but is not directly testable.
analysis_steps.evidence: CR 13, 11.1, 13.2, 10.5, and 12.6 g/U. ISF 56 mg/dL/U. DIA 10 h. All 24 therapy windows are correction boluses with no carb grams. Loop statuses show cob 0. variable_sens ranged from about 28 to 124.
analysis_steps.dependencies: basal_targets and safety_overview; Dynamic ISF later shown to override profile ISF.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: No meal-bolus traces and no clean four-hour correction without food or SMB.

analysis_steps.findings: Always-on SMB with UAM is the operating meal engine. COB-based SMB gates are idle because carbs are never entered. Frequent SMB plus UAM can explain afternoon chase and later lows, but that pattern is still mixed with DIA, DynISF, target, and evening basal.
analysis_steps.evidence: smb_enabled true, uam_enabled true, smb_always_enabled true, smb_with_cob and smb_after_carbs false, interval 3 min, max SMB 15 min, max UAM SMB 20 min. Sampled reasons include SMB 0.3 to 0.4 U and one UAM high-boost SMB 1.6 U. User temporary targets of 135 fit smb_with_high_temp_target false.
analysis_steps.dependencies: safety_overview; unused CR from profile_cr_isf_dia; afternoon TAR still meal-confounded from basal_targets.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: No complete SMB time series; sampled statuses only; extra reason-string boost logic is outside the six inventory groups.

analysis_steps.findings: Autosens is off. Dynamic ISF at 70% is the live sensitivity engine and makes peak-time ISF much stronger than 56. Max basal 12 U/h and max IOB 25 U are slack versus about 20 U/day insulin use; sampled temps were capped nearer 4 U/h. Carb-absorption settings were unused.
analysis_steps.evidence: autosens_enabled false, dynamic_sensitivity_enabled true, DynISF factor 70%. variable_sens about 27.8 to 42.5 when glucose was 245 to 262 mg/dL. sensitivity_ratio often 1, which is a neutral current ratio and not proof Autosens ran. Carb impact 8 mg/dL per 5 min and meal absorption 7 h with zero COB.
analysis_steps.dependencies: automation_smb_uam and profile_cr_isf_dia; safety_overview forbids more aggressive sensitivity.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: No Autosens histogram, expected because Autosens is disabled; no A/B of DynISF 70% versus profile ISF 56.

analysis_steps.findings: User-declared meal_strategies is an empty list, so there is no declared prebolus or immediate bolus percent to apply. Observed execution is correction-only plus SMB and UAM. Clock-hour rises look meal-like but cannot grade CR or bolus timing.
analysis_steps.evidence: analysis_context meal_strategies empty, strategy_stable_for_period null. carb_treatment_entries empty. treatment_summary total_carbs_g 0. Therapy windows are all Correction Bolus and is_extended_carbs false. Local hour 10 TAR 20.2% and hours 14 to 16 TAR 23.6 to 32.1%.
analysis_steps.dependencies: CR unused; SMB and UAM acting as the meal bolus; hypo risk after afternoon peaks.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Declared meal strategy fields are absent because meal_strategies is empty; Nightscout has no meal start stamps.

analysis_steps.findings: No e-carb entries, durations, or extended-carb flags are present. UAM is not e-carbs and is not a pump extended bolus. Absorption settings cannot be assessed.
analysis_steps.evidence: extended_carb_entries 0, carb_treatment_entries empty, all therapy windows is_extended_carbs false, loop cob 0.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: No meal-linked e-carb amount, start offset, or duration.

analysis_steps.findings: Competing explanations for the afternoon peak and evening or overnight crash are unannounced absorption with SMB UAM and DynISF stacking, a DIA 10 h insulin tail under overnight target 90, and a lesser possible contribution from 19:00 basal 0.7 U/h. The 16:00 basal 0.5 U/h and unused CR segments are not supported as primary defects. Because those causes are not separated, every profile and AAPS inventory item is kept. Safe order is hold the profile, add meal-start observation, then reconsider at most one later setting if the same pattern persists.
analysis_steps.evidence: Zero COB, TBR concentrated at local hours 19 and 0 to 3, TAR concentrated at local hours 14 to 17, DynISF variable_sens far from 56 at peaks, IOB samples near 6 U, and no clean fasting or meal-bolus tests.
analysis_steps.dependencies: All prior stages. Unresolved overlap of basal, target, DIA, SMB, UAM, and DynISF.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Meal start times with a simple bolus versus SMB-only note would separate the leading explanations more than any other single observation.

strengths: CGM coverage is 98.7% with good cadence and no invalid readings.
Overall TIR is 86.0% with mean glucose 121.6 mg/dL.
Local hours 4 to 8 are largely in range, which argues against a broad overnight basal failure.
The selected profile is complete, and historical applicability was declared yes.
Temporary targets of 135 were used and match the setting that turns SMB off for high temporary targets.
issues: Time below range is 5.1%, with local-hour TBR 18.5% at 01:00 and 15.3% at 19:00 and nadirs of 41 to 42 mg/dL.
Afternoon local hours 14 to 17 show the highest TAR, including 32.1% at 16:00.
Glucose CV is 32.6%, and some correction windows show large 120-minute falls after stacked insulin.
No carbs were logged, so CR was unused and SMB plus UAM chased unannounced rises.
Mid-period u200 profile switch, GLP-1 notes, site changes, and a 19 Aug occlusion make the 14 days less uniform.

recommendations.title: Keep the current basal profile and verify overnight lows against evening insulin
recommendations.description: Overnight TBR is real, but hours 4 to 7 are stable and afternoon TAR is not a fasting test of the 16:00 0.5 U/h segment. Residual IOB, DIA 10 h, SMB UAM, DynISF, and target 90 remain competing explanations, so no basal number is supported for change.

suggested_change.review_direction: Hold every basal segment. First check whether local 00:00-03:00 lows follow documented evening meals or high IOB rather than the 0.6 U/h overnight rate.

recommendations.title: Hold SMB, UAM, and Dynamic ISF until meal timing is recorded
recommendations.description: Always-on SMB with a 3-minute interval and DynISF 70% can chase unannounced afternoon rises and leave a long tail, but changing them now would mix with an untested profile and an empty meal declaration. This hold keeps automation after profile review and before any CR or e-carb discussion.

suggested_change.review_direction: Do not change SMB interval, UAM, or DynISF in the same step as basal, target, ISF, or DIA. Revisit at most one automation group later if meal-stamped days still show the peak-then-crash pattern.

profile_recommendation.recommendation: Keep the current basal schedule, including 0.6 U/h from 00:00 and 0.5 U/h from 16:00, and keep targets, CR, ISF, and DIA unchanged while collecting overnight observations after documented evening meal or no-meal windows.
profile_recommendation.rationale: No basal segment has a clean fasting signal. Overnight hours 4 to 7 are in range, early-night TBR overlaps residual IOB and target 90, and afternoon TAR overlaps unannounced absorption. Changing any profile row would also collide with SMB, UAM, and DynISF.
profile_recommendation.next_check: For several nights, note whether any meal or only SMB occurred after 16:00 local time and whether local 00:00-03:00 stayed out of the low range without extra carbohydrate.

parameter_decisions.rationale: Evidence: local hours 0 to 3 have TBR 10 to 18.5% but means near the 90 mg/dL target, while hours 4 to 7 are stable. Uncertainty: residual evening IOB and DIA 10 h are not separated from this rate. Dependencies: overnight target, SMB UAM, and DynISF. Change unsupported.
Evidence: local hour 5 TIR 95.2% with mean 104.2 mg/dL. Uncertainty: closed-loop temps hide the scheduled rate. Dependencies: 06:00 step and overnight IOB. No isolated dawn under-basal signal.

Evidence: local hours 6 to 7 TIR 98.7% and 98.2%. The 21 Aug 42 mg/dL near 07:19 is isolated. Uncertainty: not a fasting test. Dependencies: 05:00 step and morning meals. Raising this rate is unsafe; lowering is unsupported.
Evidence: late-morning rise coincides with breakfast-like hours and target 100. Uncertainty: meals and UAM dominate. Dependencies: unused CR 13.2 g/U and SMB always on. Not a clean basal defect.

Evidence: this is the lowest basal during the highest TAR hours, but COB is 0 and UAM is active. Uncertainty: unannounced absorption is the leading alternative. Dependencies: CR 10.5 unused, DynISF, SMB. Do not raise this segment to treat afternoon highs.
Evidence: local hour 18 already shows TBR 7.7% after the afternoon peak. Uncertainty: stacked IOB versus basal. Dependencies: 16:00 and 19:00 segments plus DIA tail. No supported change.

Evidence: local hour 19 TBR 15.3% and lows to 41 mg/dL after daytime highs. This rate is a possible co-factor, not a proven sole cause. Uncertainty: SMB UAM and DynISF stacking. Dependencies: DIA 10 h and overnight target 90. Withhold change until meal and IOB context is recorded.
Evidence: zero carb entries and cob 0, so this CR was unused. Uncertainty: no meal tests. Dependencies: SMB UAM substituting for announced carbs. Change unsupported.
Evidence: no carb treatments in this segment. Uncertainty: unused setting. Dependencies: overnight hypo risk if a later meal bolus were added here. Keep.
Evidence: morning rise is meal-like but no breakfast carbs or meal boluses were logged. Uncertainty: UAM versus CR. Dependencies: SMB always on and target 100. Cannot grade this CR.

Evidence: strongest CR sits on the worst TAR clock hour, but carbs were not entered so it did not drive the highs. Uncertainty: if meals are later bolused here, this CR is insulin-heavy beside evening TBR. Dependencies: afternoon UAM and 16:00 basal. Keep until meals are stamped.
Evidence: unused because total carbs are 0. Uncertainty: evening hypo already present from other insulin. Dependencies: 19:00 basal and overnight target. No CR change.

Evidence: correction windows are not clean ISF tests, and DynISF rewrote sensitivity to about 28 to 124. Uncertainty: u200 labeling may distort unit effect. Dependencies: DynISF 70%, SMB, DIA. Do not strengthen ISF while TBR is 5.1%.

Evidence: overnight target 90 sits on hours with double-digit TBR. Raising it could be reviewed later but is not separated from IOB tail and SMB. Uncertainty: user intent for a tight overnight target is unknown. Dependencies: 23:00 target, DIA, basal 00:00. Keep for now rather than change a dependent safety setting.

Evidence: daytime target 100 is already higher than overnight 90 and overlaps meal hours. Uncertainty: morning TAR is not proven target error. Dependencies: SMB with temporary targets and unused breakfast CR. Keep.

Evidence: this target returns to 90 before the high-TBR overnight window. Uncertainty: same confounders as the 00:00 target. Dependencies: evening basal, IOB, and SMB. Keep until overnight lows are linked to meals or IOB.

Evidence: a 10 h DIA can leave afternoon and evening insulin active at hours 0 to 3, which fits overnight TBR after daytime highs. Uncertainty: DIA is not testable here and insulin type is free_peak_oref. Dependencies: IOB display, SMB suppression, and overnight basal or target. No supported new value.

Evidence: with cob 0 this pair is the meal system and also a likely contributor to later lows. Uncertainty: turning either off is a large behavior change without meal stamps. Dependencies: activation flags, 3-minute interval, DynISF, and hypo risk. Change unsupported.

Evidence: COB gates are idle; smb_always_enabled is the active switch. High temporary targets of 135 already match high-temp SMB off. Uncertainty: no meal announcement trial. Dependencies: UAM and delivery caps. Keep the consistent activation set.

parameter_decisions.current_value: smb_interval_minutes=3 min; max_smb_basal_minutes=15 min; max_uam_smb_basal_minutes=20 min
parameter_decisions.suggested_value: smb_interval_minutes=3 min; max_smb_basal_minutes=15 min; max_uam_smb_basal_minutes=20 min
parameter_decisions.rationale: Evidence: 3-minute SMB is frequent beside TBR 5.1%, and sampled SMB sometimes exceeded a simple 15-minute times basal product. Uncertainty: extra boost logic and incomplete SMB logs. Dependencies: DynISF, max IOB, and profile ISF. Do not change delivery together with sensitivity or basal.

parameter_decisions.parameter: AAPS max basal and max IOB limits
parameter_decisions.rationale: Evidence: limits are far above about 19.7 U/day insulin and about 16.2 U/day scheduled basal. Effective temps were nearer 4 U/h, and IOB still reached about 6 U. Uncertainty: slack limits are permissive, not the overnight pattern itself. Dependencies: safety multipliers and SMB. No supported tighter numbers from this pack.

Evidence: Autosens is disabled, so target raise and lower flags are idle. DynISF 70% produced much stronger peak-time sensitivity than ISF 56. A sensitivity_ratio of 1 is a neutral current adjustment, not disabled Autosens. Uncertainty: cannot A/B DynISF versus profile ISF. Dependencies: SMB UAM and hypo cap. Keep rather than make sensitivity more or less aggressive now.
Evidence: no COB and no carb entries, so these settings were unused. Uncertainty: UAM must not be treated as COB or e-carbs. Dependencies: empty meal strategy. No absorption change.

meal_strategy_summary.suggestion: There is no declared prebolus, immediate bolus percent, or e-carb plan. Observed meals appear unannounced and are handled by UAM plus always-on SMB, with occasional corrections and sometimes a 135 mg/dL temporary target. Keep that conservative read: do not add e-carbs or retune CR until meal start times are logged, because evening and overnight hypo risk is already binding.
meal_strategy_summary.rationale: User-declared meal_strategies is empty and strategy_stable_for_period is null. Telemetry shows 0 g carbs, cob 0, and correction-only therapy windows. Afternoon TAR then evening TBR fits an unannounced-rise chase more than a CR or e-carb setting.
meal_strategy_summary.next_observation: Log afternoon and evening meal start times for several days, even without grams, and note whether a bolus or only SMB UAM followed.

exceptions.pattern: Recurring local afternoon rise around hours 14 to 17 then evening drop around hour 19, including lows near 41 to 42 mg/dL.
exceptions.suggestion: Keep the same overall no-added-bolus read for this window; if a meal is later logged here, review less stacking rather than a stronger CR or more SMB.
exceptions.rationale: This is the main peak-then-crash cluster and is still explained by UAM, DynISF, DIA, evening basal, and overnight target together.

implementation_steps: Confirm the selected AAPS profile is the one intended for review and that u200 dilution and mid-period site, sensor, GLP-1, and occlusion events are understood before any setting discussion.
Keep every profile basal, target, CR, ISF, and DIA value unchanged while the competing overnight explanations remain mixed.
Record meal start time and whether insulin came from a bolus or only from SMB UAM, especially after 16:00 local time.
Compare those notes with local 19:00 and 00:00-03:00 lows and with IOB, without changing automation in the same step.
If the same peak-then-crash pattern remains after meal stamps exist, discuss at most one later review item, choosing either an overnight target question or one SMB or DynISF question, not both.
Do not introduce e-carbs or CR edits until announced-meal traces exist.
education: Time in range near 86% can coexist with unsafe clustered lows; TBR and nadir matter more than mean glucose when reviewing overnight settings.
A sensitivity_ratio of 1 means the current adjustment is neutral. It does not mean Autosens is enabled. In this package Autosens is off and Dynamic ISF is on.
UAM detects unexplained rises. It is not a second carb count and is not an e-carb or extended pump bolus.
With DIA 10 h, afternoon and evening insulin can still be active after midnight, so overnight lows may reflect a tail rather than only the 00:00 basal rate.
Closed-loop temps and SMBs mean observed glucose is not a pure test of scheduled basal, CR, or ISF.
safety_notes: This is decision-support content only. The user must independently verify every proposed change, make changes one at a time, and monitor glucose closely. TuneMyBG prepares data for review only and does not provide medical advice.
No profile or AAPS value is proposed for change because hypoglycemia to 41 to 42 mg/dL and 5.1% TBR limit every later idea.
Do not change basal, target, ISF, DIA, SMB, UAM, or Dynamic ISF together.
High sampled IOB near 6 U versus about 20 U/day total insulin is a stacking caution, even though max IOB 25 U was not reached.
Discuss any future single-setting review with the care team before changing the pump or AAPS.
